title: Design Systems That Scale
tagline: Build a design system that 40 teams actually use: tokens, components, releases and adoption.
description: Most design systems fail quietly: a Figma library nobody trusts, a component package three versions behind, and forty shades of grey in production. This course teaches the parts that make a system survive contact with real teams: token architecture, component APIs, accessibility built into every state, versioned releases, and a governance model people accept.

You work on one system the whole way through: Northwind UI, which serves a dispatch web app and a marketing site for two brands. Your guide is Sofia Reyes, a principal product designer who has run a system used by forty teams. You write real CSS, real token files and real release plans, and you learn which decisions are expensive to undo.
audience: Designers and front-end developers who already ship UI and now need to build or run a shared design system.
prerequisites: Comfortable with HTML and CSS (custom properties, selectors), basic JavaScript, and Figma components.
learnItems: Audit an interface and decide what the system should own
Structure tokens in primitive, semantic and component tiers
Theme light, dark, density and two brands without forking code
Design component APIs that compose instead of growing props
Ship releases with semver, changelogs and painless deprecations
Run contribution, governance and adoption metrics at scale
